At any rate, it seems that a second attempt for the Port has begun, and may have even been almost completed based on the stability of things.

Signs that the Port has begun or been completed:

The order of icons by the log-off button has changed. Previous to now the My Messages envelope icon was farthest right, but now it is the lightbulb or toggling on night-mode (we won't walk about those who use the lightbulb to toggle off night-mode). This was a change that was suggested by certain testers early in the testing phases, in response to requests that have been made by Voat users for years now -- fat fingers on mobile trying to check messages too often lead to accidental log-offs. At least (decent) goats will be less likely to want to hit the lightbulb, so hopefully that's a minor issue that this minor change can resolve for lots of people.

Badges seem to be appearing in reverse order. Example: /u/MadWorld. The 4,3,2,1 badges were originally 1,2,3,4, in the order that they were given.

/v/all was temporarily "subscribable", but this has already been resolved.

If you update your profile avatar you might notice a more resolved image and clearer boundaries. I had to reupload the same file I had to get this result, but the avatars are now showing as clearly as they have been on the preview site for several weeks.

Clicking the My Messages envelope button now sends you straight to your inbox, instead of to the overview page -- if you have no messages, or only have messages of varying types. If you have notifications that are only comment replies, clicking on the envelope will send you straight to your comment replies page instead of requiring you to click on the "comment replies" button that would appear on the overview page. The only time users will be sent to the overview page, I think, is if they have, say, comment replies and subverse mail.

Submissions now have a "toggle NSFW" option, so that if you make a post and want to either add or remove the NSFW flair after the fact, submitters can do so.

Three submissions can now be stickied within a subverse at a time.
